The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that took place on 10.08.2024.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioner as follows:
On 10.08.2024 at about 5.30 p.m. when he was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-16-HL-4273 on Tumkuru Bengaluru NH-48, near Nandihalli village,
Tumkuru, at that time rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.HP-36-E-3372 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the vehicle of the petitioner,
caused the accident, due to which he sustained grievous injuries.

It is stated that he has spent huge amount for his treatment, medicine etc.,
3.
It is further stated that prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as picker at Reliance Packing and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to do his work as doing earlier.
It is stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No. HP-36-E-3372.

Hence,
the 1st respondent being the insurer and 2nd respondent being the owner of the offending motor cycle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. On service of notice, the respondent No.1 has entered its appearance through its learned counsel and filed written statement.
Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.2 remained absent and Kirana R S Alias Kiran vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149199490/

5. The 1st respondent in its objection statement has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.
It has denied the age, income and occupation of the petitioner and the amount spent towards medical expenses by the petitioner.

1st respondent has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.HP-36-E-3372 and contended that its liability is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy and valid and effective riding licence held by the rider of the motor cycle as on the date of the accident.
The compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner are excessive and exorbitant.
Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.

6. Based on the pleadings, this court has framed following issues :-
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that on 10.08.2024 at about 5.30 p.m. when he was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-16-HL-4273 on Tumkuru Bengaluru NH-48, near Nandihalli village, Tumkuru, at that time rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.HP-36-E-3372 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the vehicle of the petitioner, caused the accident, due to which he sustained grievous injuries ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3.
What order or award?
7. In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and examined a witness as PW.2 and got marked 17 documents as per Ex.P1 to 17.
On the other hand, respondents have not led its evidence.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the documents.
9.

My findings on the above issues as under:-
Issue No.1 ... Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.2 ... Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.3 ...

As per final order For the following:

sentences.text:
The petitioner in order to prove his case,
got examined himself as PW.1 and reiterated the averments of the petition and got marked F.I.R,
F.I.S, Spot Mahazar, sketch, IMV report, Wound certificate and Charge sheet as per Ex.P1 to 7.
11.

According to the version of petitioners, the accident happened near Nandihalli village, on NH-4 Tumakuru- Bengaluru, the petitioner was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-06-HL-4273 at that time rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.HP-36-E-3372 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle, due to which, petitioner fell down and caused the accident.

12. Respondent No.1 who is the insurer of the offending motorcycle bearing reg No. HP-36-E-3372 has denied the alleged negligence of the rider of the offending motorcycle and taken specific contention that the petitioner came on wrong side where the passing of the vehicle is prohibited in rash and negligently and dashed against the motorcycle of the Respondent No.2, petitioner only solely responsible for the alleged accident.
13. It is pertinent to note that, the criminal law was set in motion on the same day of accident as per Ex.P.2. Ex
. P.1 FIR has its germane in Ex.P.2.
The document which sheds light on the factum of negligence are Ex.P3 being the Spot Mahazar.

On close perusal of the Ex.P.3 and Ex.P4 which is the sketch prepared at the time of spot mahazer, on perusal of the above said documents it clearly reflects that petitioner is the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg No.KA-06-HL-4273 came on wrong side where the passing of the vehicles are prohibited and also accident occurred towards South distance of 3 feet from the North edge of the road and also width of the road is 30 feet.
Both the vehicles riders without observing the on going vehicles on the road they dashed against each other.
Added more the contents of Ex.P5 which is the IMV report itself discloses that there are no mechanical defects whatsoever in the offending vehicle as well as petitioner's motorcycle.
Even the Chargesheet as per Ex.P7 was also filed as against the petitioner and rider of the offending motorcycle/Respondent No.2.

When such is the case having regard to Ex.P3 to 5 coupled with Ex.P7 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligence driving of the Respondent No.1 as well as Petitioner.
14. It is true that both the vehicles and other users of the road are required to follow the traffic rules.

On proper perusal of the spot mahazer and sketch, it shows that petitioner came from opposite direction on one way road in wrong side where passing of vehicles is prohibited, in a negligent manner, on the other side the rider of the motorcycle bearing No. HP-36-E-3372 also came in negligent manner without observing the other vehicle, both the vehicles collided each other and accident occurred towards South from the North edge of the road at the distance of 3 feet, due to which both riders of the motorcycle fell-down along with motorcycles.

If both riders rode their vehicles in normal speed by observing on going vehicles on the road, they might have avoided the accident and also if petitioner has avoid the passing his motorcycle in wrong side and he had taken little care and follow the traffic rules in the National highway road, might have avoided collision.
The accident could have been avoided but no one has taken any care and precautions in avoiding the accident.

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

16. The discussion supra makes it is abundantly clear that, the accident occurred due to the rash negligent riding by the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.HP-36-E-3372 and the petitioner has also contributed in occurrence of the said accident.
Hence contributory negligence is attributed on the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No. No.HP-36-E-3372 and on the petitioner in the ratio of 40:60 respectively.

As such, I answer Issue No.1 as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
17. Issue No.2:
While answering issue No.1, I have already observed that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. HP-36-E-3372 and also petitioner.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation.
18. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:

It is the case of the petitioner that prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and was working as picker at Reliance packing and earning Rs.20,000/- per month and to prove the same, petitioner has not produced any documents.
In the absence of document of income, the tribunal has to consider the notional income of the petitioner.
The incident occurred during the year 2024.
considering the avocation and the year of the accident, I deem it just and proper to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,500/- per month.
The petitioner claims that he is unable to work due to the injuries sustained to him.
The petitioner got examined the Doctor as PW.2.

In the evidence of doctor, he has deposed that petitioner sustained left neck of femur fracture, left shaft of femur fracture, left patella comminuted fracture and left distal end radius fracture and underwent CRIF with Cyrus nail to left femur, ORIF with encerclage to left patella and dension band wire removal of left patella.

He examined the patient on 22.07.2025 for disability assessment and the petitioner is having pain in left lower limb and left wrist, difficulty to squat on floor, sit cross legged climb upstairs, walk on slope kneel stand on affected limb, ablution lift weight over the head with left upper limb, deformity left wrist, difficulty to do routine activities.

On radiological examination it shows the fracture femur united with implant insitu, fracture of Kirana R S Alias Kiran vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149199490/
5 patella united and left distal radius mal united.

sentences.text: He assessed 30% disability to the right left lower limb and 29% disability to left upper limb and 23% as whole body disability of the petitioner.
While calculating the loss of future income on account of permanent disability, the functional disability to the whole body has to be considered.
The disability to the whole body shall have to be assessed on the basis of the profession of the injured and relative effect of the disability to his profession.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner are not in dispute and the injuries sustained by him definitely will have an impact on his work.
PW.2 is not a treated doctor and the disability assessed by him has to be taken into consideration carefully.

Hence, considering the nature of the work and impact of disability on his performance, I deem it just and proper to consider 13%
disability to his whole body.
It is contended that petitioner was aged 21 years as on the date of accident.
The accident occurred on 10.08.2024.
However, by considering the date of birth mentioned in Ex.P8 Adhaar Card as 12.02.2003, the petitioner was aged 22 years at the time of accident.

The multiplier applicable to the age of 22 is 18 as per the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation(AIR 2009 SC 3104).

19. PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:

sentences.text: The wound certificate produced at Ex.P6 discloses the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident.

The Ex.P9 and 10 Discharge Summaries of Sapthagiri Hospital reveals that petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital from 11.08.2020 to 02.09.2024, 03.10.2024 to 05.10.2024 and and 03.06.2025 to 06.06.2025 and underwent treatment.
Considering these aspects, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.60,000/- towards pain and sufferings.

20. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has produced medical bills worth Rs.91,103/-.
I have examined the medical bills and receipts.

Further the petitioner was treated as inpatient and undergone treatment, there are no reasons to disbelieve the amount spent by the petitioner to the tune of Rs.91,103/- and he is entitled for the same.
21. ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD & NOURISHMENT AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:

sentences.text:
As the petitioner was treated as an inpatient thrice totally for a period of 29 days,
certainly he might have spent amount towards conveyance, attendant charges,
nourishing food and other incidental expenses and also at the time of subsequent follow up treatment.
Considering these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.43,500/- (1,500x29) under this head.

22. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 5 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.66,000/-
(16,500 X4) under this head.

23. LOSS OF AMENITIES IN LIFE/LIFE COMFORTS AND EXPECTANCY OF LIFE/MARRIAGE PROSPECTUS:
The petitioner was aged about 22 years at the time accident and on account of accident, he has to suffer the above disability.
He has to suffer this discomfort and sacrifice the amenities through out his remaining life.
This court has considered disability to the extent of 13% to whole body.
Considering all these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.50,000/- on this head.
24. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:
The doctor stated that the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implant.
No estimation is produced to show the future medical expenses.
Petitioner has undergone surgery of removal of implant, for which he has to necessarily bear certain expenses.

Thus he is entitled to Rs.30,000/-
towards future medical and other incidental expenses.

Interest:
The petitioner is claiming interest @ 9% p.a. on the compensation amount.

Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding future medical expenses) is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
27. Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.
HP-36-E-3372 and also on the part of the petitioner.
The breach of any of the policy conditions are not proved.

It is not disputed that 2 nd respondent is the owner and 1st respondent is the insurer,
hence they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 1st respondent being the insurer shall indemnify the 2nd respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
28. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,21,569/-(Rupees Three lakhs twenty one thousand five hundred and sixty nine only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on Rs.3,09,569/-(excluding future expenses of Rs.12,000/-) from the date of petition till its realisation.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
